doc: Ghost-checks catalog (docs/GHOST_CHECKS_PLAN.md). `protocols` — G0 inventory to invariant level; `scopes` — every atomic/ordering site in src/** and crates/*/src/** claimed by exactly one scope (scripts/ghost_inventory.mjs --check); `rules` — per-site lint rules, filled from G1 on.

protocols.name: large-THP coherent bounded estimator pair
invariants: I1 one AtomicU64 contains both Q31 estimator components; snapshot is one indivisible load
I2 a successful CAS applies exactly one accepted pure-estimator update from its expected packed pair
I3 at most eight CAS attempts per observation; exhaustion returns false without applying that observation
I4 Relaxed accesses publish no external payload; only the indivisible scalar pair is shared
protocols.real_under_loom: authored, CI pending: loom_thp_learning_cell.rs mounts the actual production cell and pure estimator on loom atomics; two different competing observations must match one complete serial order, never a torn pair or lost update
protocols.decision: rules + actual-source model + deterministic forced-CAS rejection test
protocols.reason: Task49 state foundation only; not yet admitted to runtime controls or advice. No runtime learning or performance acceptance is claimed.

protocols.name: HeapLease FREE->LIVE claim / LIVE->FREE Release drop
invariants: I1 exactly one thread wins FREE->LIVE for a slot; a losing CAS performs no metadata write, no drain and no drop
I2 every owner write to slot metadata happens-before the next claimant's first read: LIVE->FREE is a Release CAS paired with the claimant's Acquire success ordering
I3 only the lease holder mutates slot metadata between claim and drop
protocols.real_under_loom: no: HeapRegistry is a process-static built through bootstrap::ensure (OncePtrCell + chunked slots); cas_state itself is one CAS on HeapSlot::state and builds alone
protocols.reason: G3: HeapSlot::cas_state only passes the orderings through, so translating it under loom adds nothing; the orderings live at the claim/drop call sites, which need the registry bootstrap. R1 pins every cas_state call site of claim_impl, HeapLease::drop and push_back_after_oom (R4: a lost drop CAS is fatal); R8 binds the drop and claim lines of both shadow models (heap-lease/model-bind, recycle-drain/model-bind). The text pin r11_ph4a_drop_ordering_pinned is removed: its mutants turn heap-lease/drop-release and heap-lease/drop-lost-cas-fatal red.

protocols.name: MaintenanceLease FREE->MAINTENANCE
invariants: I1 a failed FREE->MAINTENANCE CAS never creates a second metadata mutator
I2 MAINTENANCE->FREE is a Release CAS; the next LIVE claimant observes every maintenance write
protocols.real_under_loom: no: same registry bootstrap as P1
protocols.reason: G4: R1 on the FREE -> MAINTENANCE claim (try_maintenance_at) and the MAINTENANCE -> FREE recycle (MaintenanceLease::drop), R4 makes a lost recycle CAS fatal; R8 binds the R8 maintenance model lines to both P2 and P1 rules. The Relaxed-drop mutant is red in the linter and, propagated to the model, a loom causality violation.

protocols.name: publish || recycle || drain (TORN stamp, trim, drop, claimant drain)
invariants: I1 a publication made before, during or after the owner's trim is consumed exactly once (trim or claimant drain) or survives pending for the next owner
I2 trim_for_recycle drains before the LIVE->FREE Release
I3 only the current lease holder drains
protocols.real_under_loom: no: drain runs through HeapCore + AllocCore segment tables
protocols.reason: G3: L1/L2 (R4b-13/14) are caught by the Ph4b model through a core cell every lease holder writes, and by R1 in claim.rs; R8 keeps the model lines equal to prod. The teardown order is R3/R4 on LeaseReleaseGuard::drop and finish_bind, the LOCAL/GUARD declarations are R10. The text pins r11_ph4b_teardown_ordering_pinned and r11_ph4b_local_no_drop_pinned are removed: their mutants turn those rules red. Exactly-once consumption under the real drain is P7/P10 (G6).
protocols.atomics: its orderings are P1 (HeapSlot::cas_state call sites) and P7 (sidecar publish/cut); trim/drain order and consumption are sequence/ghost properties (R3, ghost_event!)

protocols.name: registry claim/selector, free-set, spill, saturation
invariants: I1 count only grows (bump_count CAS) and every slot below count is initialised before it is published (initialised Release / Acquire)
I2 a free-set bit is set only after the slot is FREE (publish Release) and a taker clears it with AcqRel before claiming
I3 the summary word never hides a non-empty word (clear_summary_recheck re-publishes)
I4 saturation is monotone until publish_claimable clears it
protocols.real_under_loom: partial: FreeSlotHint and SaturationHint are self-contained structs on core atomics (translatable via #[path]); stack.rs scans walk the static registry

The stack scans stay shadow models: they walk the process-static registry.

I4 Block/BlockIndex/spare atomics are Relaxed and touched only under the shard lock

protocols.name: remote-free ingress: producer notify || owner take/arm/full drain (SC-6 A-exact)
invariants: I1 NOTIFIED => the slot bit is set in the heap mask, or its notifier is between the CAS and the summary RMW, or the owner took the bit and has not finished arm -> fence -> full drain

I2 store-buffering: producer pending fetch_or(SeqCst) then state load(SeqCst); owner state store(ARMED, Release), fence(SeqCst), then a full drain: the drain sees the bit or the producer sees ARMED and notifies
I3 ARMED is written only by the owner, after taking the slot bit, followed by the fence and a full drain
I4 NOTIFIED is written only by the producer CAS from ARMED, or at birth of a route without a heap cell
I5 after its terminal RMW the producer touches only its pinned entry state and the process-lifetime heap cell

protocols.name: large-THP tuple cell (write-once publication)
invariants: I1 single winner: one strong compare_exchange(UNSET, PUBLISHING, AcqRel, Acquire) elects the only writer
I2 the five words are Relaxed-stored by the winner before the state store(PUBLISHED, Release)
I3 the words are never written after PUBLISHED (publish is the only writer, after the claiming CAS)
I4 the loser path, read and load_words have no loop, no spin and no weak-CAS retry: a loser that meets PUBLISHING reports a conflict
I5 readers decode the words only after an Acquire load observing PUBLISHED; unpublished or PUBLISHING gives the default tuple
protocols.real_under_loom: yes: tests/loom_thp_tuple_cell.rs compiles the production thp_tuple_cell.rs (#[path]) onto the concurrency atomics; oracles: a reader never sees a torn tuple (result is exactly one candidate or the default), exactly one distinct-tuple publisher wins, a same-tuple race follows the over-count contract, and the model terminates under every interleaving (no spin)
protocols.reason: J13b #47: R1 pins every ordering (claiming CAS, PUBLISHED store, state load, word stores and loads), R3 keeps the claim before the words and the last word before PUBLISHED, R5 keeps the words and spin primitives out of every other fn, R2 closes the ordered-op inventory of publish (no spin), R4 gates both word reads on PUBLISHED; behaviour is covered by the j13b_thp_publish_* and unpublished-default integration tests and by tests/loom_thp_tuple_cell.rs, the actual-source loom model of the cell

protocols.name: large-THP budget ledger (advised bytes, bounded CAS reserve)
invariants: I1 used never exceeds the budget of a successful reservation: a reservation is one compare_exchange_weak from the observed value
I2 try_reserve loops at most MAX_ATTEMPTS times and returns 0 (no advice) when it keeps losing
I3 give_back is a single fetch_sub of the reserved bytes
I4 Relaxed is sufficient: the only shared location is used and nothing else is published through it
I5 a Large mapping is released only by release_large_mapping, which gives the charge back after the unmap
protocols.real_under_loom: yes: tests/loom_thp_ledger.rs compiles the production thp_budget_ledger.rs (#[path]) onto the concurrency atomics; oracles: racing 6 MiB reserves against an 8 MiB budget never hand out more than the budget (an unconditional fetch_add reserve fails this), grants are exact granule multiples, and the ledger is empty after every thread returns exactly its own grant
protocols.reason: J13b #47: R1 pins the Relaxed load, CAS and fetch_sub, R4 bounds the reserve loop, R3 ties the CAS to the observed value and the unmap to give_back, R5 keeps os::release_segment in the Large files inside the terminal funnel; behaviour is covered by the j13b_thp_budget_* integration tests and by tests/loom_thp_ledger.rs, the actual-source loom model of the ledger

protocols.name: large-THP deterministic control ordinal and diagnostic telemetry
invariants: I1 each next_control call obtains one successive wrapping ticket from CONTROL_ORDINAL with one fetch_add(Relaxed); the returned ticket is the ordinal input to the deterministic selection, not a publication

I2 next_control uses the fixed CONTROL_SEED with the pure decision_at(seed, ordinal) selector; the selector defines exactly one control in each complete aligned cohort of eight ordinals (not every sliding window)
I3 control counters are diagnostic wrapping u64 totals only: Relaxed accesses publish no data and establish no happens-before edge
I4 control_telemetry reads each of eight fields independently with Relaxed loads; the returned array is not a coherent multiword snapshot

I5 the bench-internals ticket log records the (ordinal, decision) actually consumed per next_control call in bounded diagnostic storage; its entries are never gate inputs and all accesses stay Relaxed
protocols.real_under_loom: no: this runtime uses process-wide core atomics; the deterministic selector is separately pure-tested, and no runtime model is claimed
protocols.reason: P26 rules pin the single Relaxed ordinal RMW, its fixed-seed decision call, and the diagnostic counter/load inventories; tests/j13b_observation_control_selector.rs checks the selector's one-control-per-complete-aligned-eight contract independently of runtime atomics

rules.reason: I2/I4: one load and one syntactic strong CAS site operate on the packed pair; no external publication
I1/I4: snapshot obtains both components from one Relaxed load of the packed pair
I3: the CAS is dominated by attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS; forced rejection terminates after eight attempts
I2: the CAS expects the observed current pair, so a competing update cannot be overwritten blindly
plan §3.1/§4.2 R9: no ghost fields in prod structs, ghost macro arguments never write, ghost:: paths outside the macros only under a ghost cfg
the last dropper must observe every other holder's accesses before it frees the Entry and sidecar: Release on every decrement, Acquire on the final one
a pin increment is a counted reference the final decrement synchronizes with
the unlink is published with Release; RoutePin::linked reads it with Acquire (cached fast path gate)
the sidecar is freed only after the early return of every non-final decrement (item 186)
free_sidecar is dominated by the reference decrement in the same or an enclosing block
only the last reference (or the constructor's own OOM rollback) frees a sidecar
the drop keeps its ghost underflow check (and the freed-once event the harness counts)
the pin keeps its ghost no-resurrection check (item 186)
the shadow model of item 186 keeps the production orderings of the decrement and the unlink
S2: every owner write to the core happens-before the next claimant; the LIVE -> FREE CAS is the Release half of that edge
a lost LIVE -> FREE CAS means a second mutator exists; the drop aborts instead of continuing
the claimant's FREE -> LIVE success ordering is the Acquire half of S2: it observes every write of the previous holder
exactly one first claimant wins EMPTY -> INITIALIZING and becomes the sole constructor of the core
a FREE slot whose core was never published is re-entered as INITIALIZING by the winner that already holds it
the constructed core is published with the LIVE state after the initialised Release store
a failed construction hands the slot back as FREE with Release; the next claimant reads initialised before choosing a path
the Ph4a shadow model keeps the production orderings of the drop and claim CAS
the Ph4b shadow model keeps the production orderings of the drop and claim CAS; its core cell makes a weakened one a loom causality violation (R4b-13/R4b-14)
the owner lease constants and exercised teardown helper bind production lease orderings and trim-before-release; bitmap behavior runs from included source
LOCAL is poisoned before any owner-side mutation of the teardown, so a later resolver never aliases the next claimant
every release of the slot (early process-exit or terminal) follows the TORN stamp
the terminal sidecar cut and cache trim run while this thread is still the sole owner; no core mutation after LIVE -> FREE
the only release that skips the trim is the process-exit early return
the GUARD-arming rollback un-publishes LOCAL before it releases the slot, so no stale published pointer outlives the lease
